newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland plans coal surcharge for '97 to aid mining.
newsitem.headline: Poland plans coal surcharge for '97 to aid mining.

text.p: The Polish government plans to introduce next year a "coal fee" to help finance the restructuring of the ailing coal industry, a deputy industry minister said on Monday.

Jerzy Markowski told a news conference the government's restructuring programme, if approved by parliament next week, would introduce for four years starting in 1997 a special surcharge on coal sales. @

He said the surcharge of 3.7 percent of net value of the transaction levied on individual buyers would fund the Katowice provincial authorities' restructuring plan for the region, while fees charged from the energy sector would finance a coal mining restructuring fund.

Markowski said the 1997 budget earmarked 748 million zlotys for costs of pit closures and the restructuring of mines which have to scale-down production. He also said the programme would cap coal price rises next year at 15 percent.
This limit would not apply to contracts with the power and energy sector, with which long-term supply agreements would be replaced with new contracts early next year, he added.
Markowski said coal output this year was expected at 136.9 million tonnes, up from 135 million tonnes. Hard coal is Poland's main source of energy.
